pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria THE SMOKING GUN: Darkening of standing urine to a port-wine color upon light exposure triggered by fasting and a cytochrome P450-inducing drug. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic defect in porphobilinogen deaminase, a key enzyme in heme synthesis. Precipitants such as starvation and CYP enzyme-inducing medications (like sulfonamides) upregulate hepatic ALAS1, causing a massive, toxic accumulation of early heme precursors (delta-aminolevulinic acid and porphobilinogen). These neurotoxic intermediates cause severe autonomic dysfunction, neurovisceral abdominal pain without physical signs of peritonitis, central nervous system disturbances, and a descending motor neuropathy that mimics Guillain-Barre syndrome.
